newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Africa human rights body adopts five-year plan.
newsitem.headline: Africa human rights body adopts five-year plan.

text.p: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (ACHPR) has adopted a five-year plan centred on increasing human rights awareness in Africa.
At the end of a 10-day meeting in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius, ACHPR said the action plan for 1996 to 2001 also aims at reinforcing reports on the countries in Africa.

"Several countries have not presented reports on human rights, probably because their situations are very bad but also possibly because they do not know the technical details requirements," said ACHPR president Isaac Nguema.
Setting up an African Court on Human Rights was also studied during the Mauritius meeting but no final decision was reached.

"The Commission was informed...that most states had not yet submitted their comments on the establishment of the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights. Therefore this issue was deferred to the OAU (Organisation of African Unity) council of ministers in February 1997," Nguema told reporters.

The Mauritius meeting also celebrated its 10th anniversary against a backdrop of worsening human rights records in certain African states especially in Burundi, Liberia, Zaire, Somalia, Nigeria and Sudan.

"Without any doubt, there have been improvements in the issue of human rights these last ten years, but we must not rejoice too quickly, as today we still see numerous dark patches on the African human rights map," said International Commission of Jurists Secretary-General Adama Dieng.

On eastern Zaire, ACHPR member Oji Umozurike said: "ACHPR calls upon Zaire and Rwanda to cease hostilities and resolve whatever differences they may have peacefully. All other parties engaged in armed and violent actions should desist so that the human rights of all can be respected."

Fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels raged near the eastern city of Goma on Thursday and aid agencies responsible for feeding more than a million Hutu refugees prepared to evacuate, aid officials said.
